subsystemMap:
ALL PATHS REPO-RELATIVE. Every automation file below is byte-identical at HEAD (bbe4575) and on disk (git diff --stat HEAD empty for scripts/lib/orion-automation-*.mjs, scripts/orion-automation*, tests/automation-*.test.mjs, plugin/orion-control/dist/automation.js, plugin/orion-control/src/automation.ts). The contracts' "context" strings use SHORT names (orion-automation-dispatch.mjs); ### READ needs the full path, e.g. scripts/lib/orion-automation-dispatch.mjs.

MODULES AND EXPORTS
1. plugin/orion-control/dist/automation.js (tracked at HEAD, 13,627 bytes; imported by schedule.mjs:3 and dispatch.mjs:6). Exports: AUTOMATION_ROOT = ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/automations (:66, PRODUCTION ROOT); AUTOMATION_ACTIONS (:76-102) is a closed table: standing_check, standing_morning, standing_evening, agenda_today {argv:["orion-agenda","today"]} (:92-96), daily_rollup; NAME_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,47}$/ (:104); MAX_AUTOMATION_DAYS = 180 (:106); validateProposal(value) -> string[] of issues (:114-195). It requires intent of 8 to 400 chars, trigger kind daily|hourly|weekly, riskLimits.maxRunsPerDay 1-1440 AND riskLimits.maxMessagesPerDay 0-48 (both required), failureBehavior stop|retry_once|report_and_continue, and permissions.expectsMode contained|guarded|open|sovereign. describeTrigger(trigger) (:197); cronExpression(trigger) (:209-218): daily "M H * * *", hourly "M * * * *", weekly "M H * * W"; simulate(proposal, options) (:233).
2. scripts/lib/orion-automation-schedule.mjs (pure preview; creates no files). export function automationSchedulePlan(proposal, timeZone, repoRoot, now = Date.now()) (:6). It runs validateProposal with a substituted future expiresOn (:9-11). It throws unless action === "agenda_today" and delivery === undefined (:12-14). It validates the timezone and policy via checkAutomationConditions on a copy with installationId "preview-only" (:15-18). It requires now to be a safe non-negative integer (:19), and expiresOn from today-in-timeZone through +180 days (:20-25). Returns (:28-40) { readyToInstall:false, nextGate:string, name:`orion-auto-${proposal.name}`, timeZone, cron, commandArgv:[join(repoRoot,"scripts/orion-automation-run"), proposal.name], policy:{action,intent,expiresOn,conditions,permissions,riskLimits,failureBehavior} (deep clones), schedulerArgs:["cron","add","--name",`orion-auto-${name}`,"--cron",cron,"--tz",timeZone,"--command-argv",JSON.stringify(commandArgv),"--command-cwd",repoRoot,"--disabled","--exact","--no-deliver","--timeout-seconds","120","--output-max-bytes","4096","--json"] }. NOTE: plan.name is the SCHEDULER job name (orion-auto-...), not the automation name. plan.policy has NO name, trigger, timeZone, installationId or installedAt. --command-cwd is the raw repoRoot string, while commandArgv[0] goes through path.join, which normalizes it (for example a trailing slash). Everything it throws is a plain Error.
3. scripts/lib/orion-automation-admission.mjs (durable daily budgets). initializeAutomationAdmission(root, record) (:71) and initializeAutomationMessages(root, record) (:72) call initializeBudget (:64-70): binding() validation, mkdir(root,{recursive:true,mode:0o700}), exclusive 'wx' create, fsync, then directory fsync. A second call rejects with code EEXIST (admission.test:78). reserveAutomationRun(root, record, context) (:73) and reserveAutomationMessage (:74) return {admitted:true, day, runNumber|messageNumber} or {admitted:false, reason}. checkAutomationConditions(record, context) (:88-91) is a pure recheck that returns {admitted:true, now, day} or {admitted:false, reason}. binding() (:14-41) validates name (NAME_RE), installationId /^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{8,80}$/ (randomUUID fits), expiresOn as a real calendar day, riskLimits.maxRunsPerDay 1-1440, permissions.expectsMode, conditions as a plain object, skipDuringFocus as a boolean when present, quietHours as [h,h] when present, and timeZone === "UTC" or a member of Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone"). Private helpers NOT exported: writeNew (:46-50), syncDirectory (:51-54), localClock (:55-61).
4. scripts/lib/orion-automation-dispatch.mjs. initializeAutomationDispatch(root, value) (:50-57) creates root/admission/<k>.json, then root/messages/<m>.json ONLY if record.delivery, then root/<k>.dispatch.json {version:1,binding,phase:"ready",lastAt:null,lastSlot:null} with 'wx'. The three steps are NOT atomic together. Any pre-existing file makes it throw EEXIST and nothing is overwritten. dispatchAutomation(root, value, scheduledAt, adapters) (:59-174). Adapters: readContext() -> {now, effectiveMode, focusActive}; authorize(action) -> must be exactly true; execute(action) -> {ok:boolean, output?, retrySafe?}; optional authorizeDelivery(message) and deliver(message). action is frozen as {name, argv, installationId} (:85-86). installation() (:14-27) requires the action to be in AUTOMATION_ACTIONS, a valid failureBehavior, installationId as a string and a valid trigger. Its binding = sha256(canonical(WHOLE record)) with object keys sorted recursively (:11-13, :26). The private helper persist (:39-49) is not exported.
5. scripts/lib/orion-automation-host.mjs. createAutomationHostChecks({repoRoot, homeRoot, run, read, now} = {}) (:23) returns frozen {readContext(), authorize(action)}. It spawns scripts/orion-authority and scripts/orion-session (:27-34) and reads ~/.openclaw state. It has no execute and no deliver (host.test:42). Tests must always inject a replacement.
6. scripts/lib/orion-automation-runtime.mjs. runInstalledAutomation(name, scheduledAt, {automationRoot = ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/automations, repoRoot = repo, checks = createAutomationHostChecks({repoRoot}), run = execFile} = {}) (:18-21). ALL FOUR DEFAULTS ARE PRODUCTION: the home root, real host probes, and a real execFile of <repoRoot>/scripts/orion-agenda today, which reads the personal calendar (:64). Tests must pass all four explicitly. It reads <automationRoot>/installed/<name>.json (:25). It requires record.name === name, action === "agenda_today", delivery === undefined, and installedAt as a Date.parse-able string (:29-31). Otherwise it returns refused/installation_unavailable_or_unsupported. It dispatches with root = <automationRoot>/runtime (:77). Its authorize = the record file is unchanged (canonical re-read) && checks.authorize (:46). Its execute (:47-75) re-checks action identity, the record being unchanged, current and admitted conditions on the same civil day, a non-regressing clock, the 5-minute window and authority again. Only then does it call run(join(repoRoot,"scripts/orion-agenda"), ["today"], {timeout:35000, killSignal:"SIGKILL", maxBuffer:1048576, encoding:"utf8", env:{...process.env, TZ:record.timeZone}}). A pre-launch refusal returns {ok:false, retrySafe:true}. A launch failure returns {ok:false}, which is never retried.
7. scripts/lib/orion-automation-tick.mjs. automationTick(args, {now = Date.now, run = runInstalledAutomation} = {}) (:5). Exactly one NAME_RE arg, else {exitCode:2, summary:{status:"refused", reason:"invalid_arguments"}}. It calls run(name, floor(now/60000)*60000) and returns {exitCode: succeeded?0:1, summary:{status[, reason matching /^[a-z_]{1,80}$/]}}. On a throw it returns runtime_unavailable.
8. scripts/lib/orion-automation-removal.mjs. removeAutomationSchedule(run, binary, name) (:3-30) runs `cron list --all --json`, expects {jobs:[{id,name,...}], total === jobs.length, offset:0, hasMore:false} with unique ids, then `cron remove <id> --json`, then lists again. It returns {removed:false, alreadyAbsent:true} or {removed:true, alreadyAbsent:false, id}, and throws otherwise. This is the ONLY evidence at HEAD of the real scheduler's read-back format. It contains no enabled/cron/tz/argv fields.
9. scripts/orion-automation (human CLI, 182 lines): list/show/simulate/schedule-plan/install/remove. install deliberately refuses (:153-157). remove turns installed/<name>.json back into proposed/<name>.json, deleting installedAt and cron (:159-179). Its binary is ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw (:60). It is not in any task scope.
10. scripts/orion-automation-run (6 lines): prints JSON.stringify(automationTick(argv).summary) and sets the exit code.

DATA FLOW
The chain is: proposal, then automationSchedulePlan (pure), then [THIS BATCH: scripts/lib/orion-automation-install.mjs, which does not exist at HEAD: verifyDisabledSchedule, installDisabledAutomation, reconcileDisabledAutomation], then the installed record at <root>/installed/<name>.json plus ledgers at <root>/runtime, then (future, not this batch) the real scheduler job running commandArgv in cwd repoRoot, then automationTick, then runInstalledAutomation, then dispatchAutomation.
Inside dispatchAutomation the steps are, in order:
- installation() and binding;
- scheduledSlot, which requires scheduledAt % 60000 === 0 and a match with the trigger in record.timeZone (:28-38);
- mkdir lock <k>.dispatch.json.lock, where EEXIST gives busy_or_unavailable;
- state validation.
Each attempt then does: readContext (now must lie in [scheduledAt, scheduledAt+300000], :99); authorize; reserveAutomationRun(<root>/runtime/admission); persist phase "pending"; execute. The result then goes to a phase transition.

VERIFIED INSTALLED-RECORD ASSEMBLY (probe run today in a scratch temp dir)
record = {name: proposal.name, installationId: randomUUID(), installedAt: new Date(now).toISOString(), timeZone: plan.timeZone, trigger: proposal.trigger, ...plan.policy}. Passed to initializeAutomationDispatch(join(root,"runtime"), record) and written as JSON to root/installed/<name>.json, it gave: runInstalledAutomation succeeded once, and the identical trigger was then refused duplicate_or_old_trigger with 1 launch. The same shape is the fixture at tests/automation-runtime.test.mjs:13-16. The record given to initializeAutomationDispatch must be canonically IDENTICAL to what is published, because the dispatch binding hashes the whole record. Any extra, missing or changed field (including installedAt or intent), or a later edit to the file, makes every dispatch refuse with invalid_state.
runtimeFormats:
ON-DISK LAYOUT UNDER A ROOT (the runtime's automationRoot; the contracts' `root`):
- <root>/installed/<name>.json: the installed record. The runtime reads it at runtime.mjs:25-34; the CLI list reads trigger and expiresOn (orion-automation:100-103).
- <root>/proposed/<name>.json: CLI proposals only (orion-automation:58, :115).
- <root>/runtime/: created by initializeAutomationDispatch through mkdir recursive, mode 0o700 (admission.mjs:66).
- <root>/runtime/<k>.dispatch.json, where k = sha256(installationId) hex (dispatch.mjs:26). Shape: {version:1, binding:sha256(canonical record), phase, lastAt:null|ms, lastSlot:null|"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", lastDelivery?}. phase is one of ready | pending | stopped | action_completed | delivery_pending | delivery_unknown (:72-77). After a success: {"version":1,"binding":"...","phase":"ready","lastAt":1789909500000,"lastSlot":"2026-09-20T09:05","lastDelivery":"not_requested"} (observed).
- <root>/runtime/<k>.dispatch.json.lock/: a DIRECTORY lock held during a dispatch (:65-67), removed in finally (:173). If a process dies, it stays and later dispatches are refused busy_or_unavailable.
- <root>/runtime/admission/<k>.json, same k. Shape: {version:1, binding:sha256(JSON.stringify(policy subset of name, installationId, timeZone, expiresOn, maxRunsPerDay, expectsMode, quietHours, skipDuringFocus)), day:null|"YYYY-MM-DD", runs:int, lastAt:ms}. Initial: {version:1,binding,day:null,runs:0,lastAt:0} (admission.mjs:67-68).
- <root>/runtime/admission/<k>.lock/: a directory lock during a reservation. It is never auto-removed (:148-151).
- <root>/runtime/messages/sha256("messages:"+id).json: only when record.delivery is present. That never happens on the agenda_today runtime path, because the runtime refuses delivery.

Durable-write conventions to mirror (private helpers; install.mjs cannot import them):
- Create exclusively with open(file,"wx",0o600), writeFile, handle.sync(), close, then fsync the directory (admission.mjs:46-54, dispatch.mjs:39-49).
- Replace with a temp file `${file}.${randomUUID()}.tmp` written "wx", then rename over the target, fsync the directory, and unlink the temp in finally.
- Locks are mkdir(lockDir,{mode:0o700}). EEXIST means busy. A lock is NEVER treated as stale (admission.mjs:149-151). Tests remove a lock only after positively observing that the child exited (dispatch.test:175-177, admission.test:178-181).
- Missing or corrupt state is never re-created by the runtime (admission.test:105-113, runtime.test:62-65). A consumed reservation is never refunded (admission.mjs:142-143).

RESULT VOCABULARY
- dispatchAutomation / runInstalledAutomation status: succeeded | refused | failed | outcome_unknown.
- Refusal reasons from the runtime: invalid_name, installation_unavailable_or_unsupported.
- Refusal reasons from dispatch: invalid_installation, not_due, busy_or_unavailable, invalid_state, outcome_unknown (phase pending), stopped, action_completed, delivery_pending, delivery_unknown, duplicate_or_old_trigger, stale_or_future_trigger, not_authorized, state_or_adapter_unavailable.
- Admission reasons: invalid_policy, invalid_clock, mode_mismatch, expired, quiet_hours, focus_active, focus_unknown, busy, state_unavailable, invalid_state, clock_regressed, daily_limit.
- Refusal before any execution: {status:"refused", reason, attempts:0}. The ledger stays ready and no quota is consumed (dispatch.mjs:88-94).
- A pre-launch refusal INSIDE runtime execute (record changed, conditions or authority changed during the final probe) returns {ok:false, retrySafe:true}. Under failureBehavior "stop" the result is {status:"failed", attempts:1} with phase stopped, and the injected run is never called (runtime.test:66-92).
- A launched failure is {ok:false}, giving outcome_unknown and phase stopped. A later dispatch returns reason "stopped" (runtime.test:93-102, 111-120).
- Process death after "pending" leaves the lock. After the lock is removed, the dispatch returns reason outcome_unknown (dispatch.test:160-180).
- skipDuringFocus:true requires focusActive === false exactly. null or undefined gives focus_unknown; true gives focus_active (admission.mjs:111-113).
- Expiry is inclusive through expiresOn in record.timeZone (admission.mjs:105).
- runInstalledAutomation on success calls checks.readContext twice and checks.authorize twice (runtime.test:44).

TICK/CLI
- orion-automation-run prints {"status":...,"reason"?} with exit code 0 (succeeded), 1 (otherwise) or 2 (invalid args) (tick.mjs, schedule.test:72-77).

SCHEDULER SHAPES
- The contracts define an injected adapter: createDisabled(plan), read(id), remove(id).
- The contracts define a normalized observed object: {id,name,timeZone,cron,commandArgv,cwd,enabled,exact,noDeliver}.
- For verification, the expected values come from automationSchedulePlan output: expected.name = "orion-auto-<name>", expected.timeZone, expected.cron, expected.commandArgv. The expected cwd is schedulerArgs[schedulerArgs.indexOf("--command-cwd")+1].
- The only real read-back format in the repo is removal.mjs's list {jobs:[{id,name}],total,offset,hasMore}. The real enabled/cron/tz/argv fields are NOT established anywhere at HEAD, and .builds/ CLI-help evidence is gitignored and absent from the worktree.
- Production constants the tests must never touch: ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/automations, ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw, <repo>/scripts/orion-agenda, scripts/orion-authority, scripts/orion-session.
testConventions:
Runner and reporter:
- Each suite starts `import test from "node:test"; import assert from "node:assert/strict";` (line 1-2 of all seven tests/automation-*.test.mjs).
- Tests are flat top-level test(name, fn) calls. There is no describe.
- Node here is /opt/homebrew/bin/node v26.5.0. The check runs node --test with the default spec reporter, which prints one line per test, e.g. "✔ name (ms)". Failure details are printed AFTER all test lines under "✖ failing tests:".
- The existing automation-tests check passes 82/82 in about 3.1 s with about 7 KB of output. Verified today, using the check's exact argv and environment.
- Assertions pin exact values: assert.equal on reason strings, assert.deepEqual on argv and call lists (schedule.test:16, host.test:33-37, removal.test:22-26), assert.rejects/throws for refusals, and counts of executions or launches as negative proof (dispatch.test:26, runtime.test:60).

Temp roots:
- `const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "orion-<suite>-")); t.after(() => rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true }));` appears at runtime.test:11-12, dispatch.test:15-16, admission.test:17-18, delivery.test:16-17 and host.test:118-119. The callback form is `async t => {...}`.
- Pure functions get fake absolute paths instead of real ones: "/fixture/repo with spaces" (schedule.test:14), "/fixture/repo" and "/fixture/home" (host.test:12-18).

Fixtures and fakes:
- Factory functions return fresh objects: `const policy = () => ({...})` at dispatch.test:11-13, admission.test:12-14 and schedule.test:8-11. The last is the canonical proposal fixture: name "calendar-check", intent, agenda_today, trigger daily 9:05, conditions {}, expectsMode guarded, riskLimits {maxRunsPerDay:2, maxMessagesPerDay:0}, failureBehavior stop.
- fixture(t, change) spreads overrides (runtime.test:10-40).
- Adapters are object literals of async closures that push into a calls array and read mutable host state (dispatch.test:18-24, runtime.test:21-38).
- runtime.test adds a `beforeContext(count)` hook to mutate state between the first and second context read (runtime.test:26, 73, 79-81, 89).
- A scripted-response fake shifts from a queue, asserts `responses.length` so an unexpected call fails, and throws queued Errors (removal.test:7-16).
- Variations are looped inside one test (runtime.test:53-57, 86-91; schedule.test:42-47).

Clock injection:
- Fixed instants such as `Date.parse("2026-09-20T10:00:00Z")` (runtime.test:9, dispatch.test:10, delivery.test:10).
- automationSchedulePlan takes `now` as a NUMBER, 4th argument (schedule.test:30-39).
- automationTick and createAutomationHostChecks take `now` as a FUNCTION (schedule.test:51, host.test:18).
- dispatch, admission and runtime get time only from readContext().now.
- The existing schedule tests also use real Date.now() + 7 days for expiresOn (schedule.test:9).
- The machine timezone is Europe/London (verified). Existing zones used: UTC, Europe/London, America/Los_Angeles, Asia/Tokyo.

Child processes:
- `promisify(execFile)(process.execPath, ["--input-type=module","-e", source, JSON.stringify(args)])`. The source imports the real module through `new URL("../scripts/lib/<module>.mjs", import.meta.url).href` and uses inline fakes; functions cannot cross the process boundary, only JSON arguments (admission.test:22-28, dispatch.test:160-197, delivery.test:138-153).
- Death is simulated by process.exit(73) inside an adapter. It is asserted with `await assert.rejects(p, error => error.code === 73)`. stdout is parsed with JSON.parse(result.stdout).
- Builtin fault injection is done in the CHILD: `import fs from 'node:fs/promises'`, patch fs.rename or fs.open, `syncBuiltinESMExports()`, then dynamically `await import(moduleURL)` (admission.test:131-159, dispatch.test:198-219). This works because the modules import named bindings from "node:fs/promises".
- The real entrypoint is run as a subprocess at schedule.test:72-77.
- Disposable shell scripts are written into the temp root with mode 0o700 to stand in for scripts/orion-agenda (runtime.test:104-106, 112-116).

Rules this environment imposes on tests:
- The worker's checkpoint verifier refuses a dirty worktree: untracked files count (workspace.mjs:72-88, worker.mjs:395-396). Tests must write only under os.tmpdir() and must not leave files in the repository.
- The reviewer re-runs every check, and any pass/fail disagreement voids the checkpoint (reviewer.mjs:64-82). Tests must be deterministic: fixed clocks, no wall-clock races, no dependence on today's real date.
- Tests must not print to the console.
- Never put the strings ENOENT, "No such file or directory" or "command not found" (any case) in test names, messages or output. See workerMechanics: they turn a check UNUSABLE and block the task for a human, even when it passes.
workerMechanics:
Source files are read from the ON-DISK host code, which is what runs. Several of these agentic files are uncommitted or untracked, but that does not matter for the worktree.

PROMPT (prompts.mjs:137-154). Each turn is rebuilt from scratch in this order:
- renderContract (:43-74): Title, Objective, Risk, Review depth, Context, Scope, Non-scope, constraints, Preconditions, Acceptance, Checks as descriptions, Escalate if;
- then the brief, appended by renderBrief (:83-89) under the heading "## BRIEF — reference for this task" (NOT "### Brief"). The heading is followed by the italic line "...it grants nothing. Scope, acceptance and non-scope above still govern — if the brief seems to disagree with them, follow the contract and say so with ### PROPOSE.";
- then "## WHY THIS TASK CAME BACK" feedback, operator instructions, "## FILES IN YOUR WORKING SET", "## CHECK RESULTS" (the last 6000 chars of each check's output, :98-107), "## NOTICE" and "## YOUR TURN".
No earlier reasoning or earlier turns are carried over.

BRIEF LOADING (plan.mjs:32-75)
- The folder <plan>.briefs/ holds common.md plus <task-id>.md. It may contain only .md files named common or a real task id; an orphan id, an empty file, or any other file throws.
- brief = common + "\n\n---\n\n" + own (:67). The combined length must be ≤ MAX_BRIEF = 18,000 chars (contract.mjs:65), counted after trim.
- The brief is part of the contract digest (contract.mjs:218), and correction tasks inherit the parent's brief (orion-project-agent.mjs:523-541, 572). common.md must therefore stay true for correction tasks too.
- Task 5's own brief shares this budget with common.md.

BUDGETS
- Worker: contextTokens 65536, maxOutputTokens 16000, think:true, temperature 0.2 (models.mjs:55-64). Input budget = 65536-16000-1024 = 48,512 tokens, estimated at 3 UTF-8 bytes per token (context.mjs:30-55), so about 145.5 KB for the system prompt plus the turn. worker-system.md is 7,702 bytes, a rendered contract 3.0-3.6 KB (measured), and the brief up to 18 KB. Multibyte characters such as the em dash cost 3 bytes each.
- num_predict 16000 covers thinking AND the answer. A reply must hold complete files, so large files may not fit alongside the reasoning. A hit output limit produces doneReason 'length' (worker.mjs:217-219) or a FILE block with no closing fence, which is MALFORMED.
- 14 exchanges per attempt (worker.mjs:36). maxAttempts 3 (plan options; models.mjs limits).
- Attempt timeout taskTimeoutMs = 60 min (models.mjs:101; applied per worker call, orion-project-agent.mjs:938). A timeout goes to the reviewer.

WORKING SET
- At most 8 files (worker.mjs:37). Each file is truncated at 90,000 chars (:38, :259).
- Initial set = the scope files that exist (:73-81). Tasks 1 and 5 start EMPTY; tasks 2-4 start with the two committed scope files.
- A ### READ of a path already in the set is ignored and does not refresh it (:257). When there are more than 8 files, the oldest are dropped (:261). fitWorkingSet evicts the oldest first when over budget (context.mjs:74-83).
- Reads are not scope-limited but deny-listed: var/brain/, var/data/, .env*, keys, .git/ (boundary.mjs:88-99).
- The worktree is built from HEAD. At HEAD these are ABSENT: scripts/lib/orion-automation-install.mjs, tests/automation-install.test.mjs, docs/planning/v2/PHASE_57_LOCAL_AGENT_REVIEW.md, and the plan itself (docs/agentic/plans/advance-orion-capabilities.md is untracked). .builds/ is gitignored.
- AGENTS.md at HEAD is 47,073 bytes and HANDOFF.md 93,611 bytes. Reading either costs a third to two-thirds of the whole input budget and evicts code.

MARKERS (prompts.mjs:185, case-sensitive, at the start of a line, optional colon)
- ### READ, ### SEARCH, ### FILE, ### CHECK, ### DONE, ### BLOCKED, ### PROPOSE, ### SUBTASK.
- A marker is recognised ANYWHERE at the start of a line, including inside reasoning prose. A prose line starting "### DONE" is a DONE.
- ### FILE: <path> is followed by the first ```lang\n ... ``` block. The regex is lazy up to the FIRST following ``` (:206). A file whose content contains ``` anywhere is therefore silently TRUNCATED, which matters for the Markdown review packet. A missing path or a missing fence is MALFORMED and produces a notice.
- The body of a FILE ends at the next marker line, so file content must not contain lines starting "### READ|SEARCH|FILE|CHECK|DONE|BLOCKED|PROPOSE|SUBTASK".
- Files are complete files only (worker-system §2). The write limit is 2 MiB (workspace.mjs:159). Writes pass the scope gate first (boundary.mjs:185-201). All three scope paths are allowed by both the installed and repo self-change policy (verified).
- ### SEARCH runs git grep -F with a literal string, at most 3 matches per file and 40 in total, each line cut to 300 chars (workspace.mjs:331-341).

CHECKS (checks.mjs)
- Fixed argv only, run with cwd = worktree.
- node-syntax (:37-43): node --check on each CHANGED .mjs/.js. Passes as "no matching changed files" when there are none.
- automation-install-tests (:63-68): node --test tests/automation-install.test.mjs, 5 min timeout. Before the file exists the output is "Could not find 'tests/automation-install.test.mjs'", exit 1, a normal FAIL (verified).
- automation-tests (:69-77): node --test on the seven suites, 10 min timeout.
- Environment (:126-136): PATH fixed, real HOME, real TMPDIR, CI=1, ORION_AGENTIC_CHECK=1, ORION_REPO_ROOT=worktree.
- HAZARD: environmentBroken (:189-192) marks ANY result, passing or failing, UNUSABLE if the first 2000 chars of its output match /command not found|ENOENT|No such file or directory/i. runChecks then stops (:277-285), and the worker throws WorkerBlocked humanOnly (worker.mjs:319-324), which blocks the task for Nick. Verified: a short failing node:test suite whose error is an fs ENOENT prints "Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory" within the first 2000 chars. A test NAME containing those words appears in the first lines even on a pass.

PROGRESS AND STUCK GATE (worker.mjs:141-142, 272-353)
- barren counts turns that wrote a file, sent CHECK or sent DONE. Pure READ/SEARCH turns neither count nor reset.
- Progress means writing a path not yet written THIS attempt, or some check going fail to pass. Progress sets barren = 0, then the end of the same turn adds 1.
- barren ≥ 4 (stuckAfterTurns, models.mjs:92) throws stuck and the task goes to the reviewer. So after the last progress turn only 3 more write/check turns without progress are allowed. Rewriting an already-written file is NOT progress.
- Repetition: an action fingerprint of kind:path/target:content-digest seen 3 times in one attempt means blocked (:226-230). SUBTASK labels and DONE text are NOT in the fingerprint, so a bare ### CHECK (or SUBTASK + CHECK), or a bare ### DONE, sent three times in an attempt ends the attempt.

SELF-REVIEW CHECKPOINTS (:121-122, 152-206). One per distinct cause, per attempt. Causes: a SUBTASK n/m change after the first, a check flipping either way, the same failure output twice, any written file over 12,000 chars (:280), or a high-risk write. On the next exchange ### DONE is withheld; READ, FILE and CHECK still work. A DONE in the same turn a trigger fires is deferred with "Self-review is required before committing." (:355).

DONE ACCEPTED ONLY IF (:355-378) and then the verifier (:392-403):
- the turn has no checkpoint;
- at least one file was written this attempt;
- checks are fresh (a DONE with stale checks runs them automatically, :296);
- every contract check is ok;
- the commit of the written paths succeeds;
- the verifier finds a clean worktree, HEAD equal to the commit, and every named check passing.

BLOCKED means humanOnly (:232-233). PROPOSE is recorded only (:234-238).

ATTEMPTS
- A new attempt starts from the last known checkpoint: git reset --hard plus clean -fd (supervisor.mjs:416, workspace.mjs:269-279). Uncommitted files from the failed attempt are GONE; the worker only sees feedback text.
- A reviewer repair keeps the work (supervisor.mjs:398).

reviewerMechanics:
REVIEW (reviewer.mjs:48-132; prompt at prompts.mjs:156-168; system at prompts/reviewer-system.md)
- The same model as the worker: qwen3.6:27b, contextTokens 65536, maxOutputTokens 12000, think:true, temperature 0.1 (models.mjs:77-81). Input budget = 52,512 tokens, about 157.5 KB.
- The reviewer RE-RUNS all contract checks itself before judging (reviewer.mjs:64-85). If any result disagrees with the worker's claim, it throws ReviewUnusable ("broken checkpoint"). Flaky tests are fatal.
- Reviewer evidence carries only {name, ok, ms, exitCode}, with NO output (:83). Its CHECK RESULTS section therefore shows "(no output)", and it never sees test names except in the diff.
- The prompt is the full contract plus the BRIEF (same renderContract), then "WHAT THE WORKER SAYS IT DID" (DONE text of at most 2000 chars), then "DIFF UNDER REVIEW" for THIS checkpoint only (diffForCheckpoint, truncated at 60,000 chars, workspace.mjs:296-310), then check results and prior findings.
- The reviewer CANNOT read files. The contract, the brief and the diff are all it knows about the existing API, so the brief is the reviewer's only source for runtime formats. Anything phrased as a requirement in the brief may be enforced by the reviewer as if it were acceptance.
- Output is one JSON block: verdict PASS | PASS_WITH_TASKS | BLOCKED; summary; examined; passed; failed[{criterion, severity minor|major|blocking, evidence}]; corrections[{title, objective, acceptance[], context}]; escalationReason and escalationKind for BLOCKED (reviewer-system.md:107-148).
- PASS may carry no major or blocking failure. PASS_WITH_TASKS requires corrections. Corrections inherit and may only narrow the scope. Malformed output is retried once (MAX_REVIEW_ATTEMPTS 2).
- reviewer-system §1 says to judge against acceptance, scope, non-scope and constraints, not taste. §5 says a broken environment is BLOCKED approval/judgement, never the worker's fault.

REPAIR (reviewer.mjs:139-214; prompts.mjs:170-179; prompts/reviewer-repair.md)
- Triggered after a stuck, timed-out or repeatedly failing worker.
- The prompt is contract plus brief, history, the full contents of up to 6 scope files (90 KB each), the current diff, and check results. It has no READ or SEARCH ability.
- Replies use the same ### FILE complete-file format, parsed by the same parseWorkerReply, so the triple-backtick truncation hazard applies.
- At most 2 files (DEFAULT_MAX_REPAIR_FILES, :38; repairMaxFiles, models.mjs:97). More files escalate to architecture.
- The repair writes through the same scope gate, runs the checks, and returns {diagnosis, changed, rationale, remaining, escalate}.
- reviewer-repair.md forbids changing tests to make them pass, changing the architecture, or touching more than a handful of files. An architectural fix means escalating instead.
- Work is kept (keepWork) and committed as a separate "agent-repair" commit.
- Budget risk: both full scope files plus a diff of up to 60 KB plus the brief must fit in about 157 KB. assertPromptFits throws rather than trimming (context.mjs:57-65, models.mjs:372), so very large scope files can make repair impossible.

FINAL REVIEW (reviewer.mjs:233-260): the combined diff of the whole run, up to 90,000 chars. The brief is not included.
repoRules:
From `git show HEAD:AGENTS.md` (786 lines, 47,073 bytes). Only the rules that bear on writing this Node code, its tests and the review doc:

1. Consumers must be tested on what producers actually emit (:472-477). "If module B consumes module A's output, at least some of B's fixtures must come from calling A." So installer and route fixtures should come from automationSchedulePlan, initializeAutomationDispatch and runInstalledAutomation, not hand-built stand-ins. This matches the task 4 contract.
2. A mechanism that verifies itself against itself always passes (:596-606). This matches task 1's "Do not validate an object against itself". Expected values must come from an independent source.
3. Pin contents, not counts (:607-613). Assert exact argv arrays and exact reasons, not lengths.
4. Check a writer's actual return vocabulary; do not guess it (:544-549). Use the exact reason and status strings listed in runtimeFormats.
5. A guard on a function is not a guard on the type, and a second constructor is a second door (:488-496, :626-634). Grep every path that builds or mutates the same record.
6. Never truncate an identifier that is compared for equality (:635-640).
7. A default is not a ceiling; clamp at the boundary (:641-645).
8. An empty filter must deny, not admit (:650-652).
9. A test that injects a timezone equal to the machine's proves nothing (:653-662). This machine is Europe/London (verified). A day is not 86,400 s, so beware DST (:693-697).
10. House style (:784-786): prefer small files of 200-400 lines typical; comments explain WHY, especially why an obvious alternative was rejected. Existing automation modules follow this with dense header comments.
11. Rules the worker must NOT act on, because they are out of scope or impossible:
- "Write before you finish: append a dated section to HANDOFF.md" (:161-173). HANDOFF.md is in no task's scope.
- "run date before any dated write" (:147-159). The worker has no shell. Do not write dates or commit ids you did not observe.
- "Read HANDOFF.md first" (:11-15).
- commit and push rules (:711-779). The host commits.
12. Secrets: .env* files are untracked and deny-listed (:776-779; boundary.mjs:61, 91). The secret-scan check is not in this plan.

Not repo rules: the user's private ~/.claude rules (immutability, no console.log) apply to Claude, not the worker, and existing modules mutate state objects freely (e.g. dispatch.mjs:107, 116). The brief should not impose them.

planLevelIssues.detail: Checkpoint and review mechanics constrain test design in ways the contracts do not mention. (a) The verifier refuses a dirty worktree, and untracked files count, so tests must never leave files in the repository. (b) The reviewer re-runs every check, and any disagreement voids the checkpoint, so tests must be deterministic: fixed clocks, no dependence on the real date or on timing. (c) The reviewer cannot read files and sees check results without output, so the test diff and the brief are its only evidence. None of this adds a requirement; it determines whether a correct task can be accepted.
